note: First draft, written from knowledge.json and the real feed (feedback/instagram-audit.json). Edit freely: the ads brief shows whatever is here. Every line must be something a real person can say or film. A number is only allowed if it is in knowledge.json or read off the screen during the shoot. Lines in [square brackets] are prompts for the person on camera, not a script.

ideas.title: Same swing, two clubs
ideas.who: One real customer hitting, a fitter talking

hook.say: Same golfer. Same swing. Two different clubs.
hook.show: Two swings back to back: the club they walked in with, then the fitted one. The TrackMan screen after each.

points: This is the club they walked in with.
This is the same swing with a shaft that suits it.
Read the numbers off the screen yourself. That is what a fitting is.
shots: Side-on swing with their own club, then the TrackMan screen
The fitter changing the shaft
Side-on swing with the fitted club, then the screen again
The golfer's face when they see the second set of numbers
ideas.watch_out: Use the real numbers from the session. If the difference is small, say so. Never a made-up number.

ideas.title: When last did anyone check?
ideas.who: A fitter to camera, a customer's own clubs

hook.say: When last did anyone check if your clubs fit you?
hook.show: A golfer's own clubs laid out on the fitting bench. The fitter picks one up and looks down the shaft.

points: Most golfers buy first and hope it fits. We do it the other way round. Fit first. Buy second.
We measure your swing on TrackMan and change one thing at a time.
You see every number yourself. Nothing is a mystery.
shots: Their own clubs on the bench
A swing on TrackMan, side on
The screen with the real numbers
The shaft wall, hand reaching for one
ideas.watch_out: Never make the golfer feel stupid for the clubs they have. Curious, not critical.

ideas.title: What happens in a fitting
ideas.who: A fitter walking the viewer through the studio

hook.say: Here is what actually happens in a fitting at Stick.
hook.show: The camera walks in through the studio door in Paarl and the fitter turns to greet it.

points: You bring your own clubs and hit a few, so we can see where you are today.
Then we change one thing at a time and watch what the ball does.
The workshop builds what the numbers pointed to.
shots: Walking in through the door
Warm-up swings with their own club
The shaft wall
The TrackMan screen
Hands at the workshop bench
ideas.watch_out: One continuous walk if you can. It should feel like being shown around, not a list.

ideas.title: Not good enough to get fitted?
ideas.who: A fitter straight to camera, club in hand

hook.say: "I'm not good enough to get fitted." Let's talk about that.
hook.show: The fitter close to camera in the studio, holding a club across both hands.
hook.text: Not good enough to get fitted?

points: A fitting is not a test. Nobody is marking your swing.
We fit the swing you have today, not the one you wish you had.
You will understand every number before you leave.
shots: Fitter to camera, eye level
A relaxed customer mid-session, laughing or nodding
A hand pointing at one number on the screen
ideas.watch_out: Warm, not preachy. The joke is shared with the golfer, never on them.

ideas.title: Roll a few
ideas.who: A fitter handing a putter to a real customer

hook.say: Roll three putts with this and tell me what you feel.
hook.show: A putter passed from one hand to another. Close on the face, then the ball rolling.

points: [Fitter: the first thing you check when you fit a putter, in your own words.]
[Customer: what felt different, straight after the third putt.]
Come roll a few and feel the difference for yourself.
shots: The hand-over
Low behind the ball as it rolls
Close on the putter face at address
The customer's reaction
ideas.watch_out: Let the customer answer honestly. Keep whatever they say.

ideas.title: Why it's here
ideas.who: Whoever chose to stock it, product in hand

hook.show: The product held up on the shop floor. Title frame over it.

points: [One sentence: what it is.]
[The one reason Stick made space for it. Not the catalogue description.]
[Who it suits, and who it doesn't.]
shots: Product in hand on the shop floor
One close detail: the stitching, the face, the logo
Someone using or wearing it
Where it sits on the shelf
ideas.watch_out: One product per video. If the reason is not honest, pick another product.

ideas.title: Where the numbers get built
ideas.who: The club builder at the bench

hook.say: This is where the numbers get built.
hook.show: Hands working on a club at the workshop bench, close.

points: After the fitting, the spec goes to the bench.
[Builder: the job on the bench right now, and why it matters.]
Every club is built to the spec you were fitted for.
shots: Close on hands and tools
The spec sheet or the screen it came from
The finished club held up to the light
ideas.watch_out: Real work on a real club. No staged tapping.

ideas.title: In their words
ideas.who: A real customer, filmed straight after their session

hook.say: [Customer, to camera:] I thought my clubs were fine.
hook.show: The customer in the studio holding the club they came in with.

points: [What did you walk in with, and what did you expect?]
[What surprised you?]
[What would you tell a friend who is thinking about it?]
shots: Customer to camera, chest up, studio behind them
A cutaway to one of their swings
A cutaway to the screen
ideas.watch_out: Their words, not a script. If they say a number it must be the one that was on the screen.

ideas.title: The product arrives by itself
ideas.who: Nobody. The product is the character

hook.say: No voice. Music or shop sound only.
hook.show: A still of the product that moves as if someone is wearing or carrying it: the pants walk in and stop at the counter, the bag unzips itself, the cap tips.
hook.text: The product name, then: Available now at Stick.

points: One movement, start to finish. Not three.
The product stays sharp and true to colour the whole time.
End on the still product and the line: Available now at Stick.
shots: One clean product photo on a plain or in-store background
The same photo with room around it for the movement
ideas.watch_out: Retail only. It has to move; a flat photo is not an ad.
